evidence.note: Revised DB schema from storing secret hashes to cleartext secrets after recognizing hashes make SigV4 verification impossible — a design revision on a falsified foundational assumption.

Presigned SigV4 failures: built a standalone reference signature computation, added debug logging, compared against server, and isolated the real signing-rule bug (ignoring X-Amz-Date from query params). Treated verification failure as signal about the signing rule.

Multipart completion failures: rejected surface hypotheses (ETag quotes, unread body) and found the real cause — namespaced boto3 XML defeating findall. Built _ns_strip and propagated it to all XML config handlers, then re-verified tagging/versioning were also fixed. Root-cause fix propagated across dependents.
Diagnosed health-endpoint 404 as FastAPI catch-all route ordering and restructured route registration — fixing actual cause.
Terminal/server went silent and the agent itself enumerated known unfixed bugs, yet submitted 'complete' three times without re-verifying — ignoring contradicting evidence at the finish.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly went beyond surface patches: on the presigned signing rule, the XML-namespace class of failures, and secret storage it treated verification failures as signal about a foundational assumption and revised the design, notably propagating the _ns_strip fix across all XML handlers and re-verifying dependents (anchor-8 behavior). It falls short of 8-10 overall because much of its course-correction was recovery from self-inflicted file corruption rather than proactive de-risking, the adaptation was reactive rather than anticipatory, and at the end it ignored clear contradicting evidence (silent output / probable crash, plus its own list of unfixed bugs) and submitted as complete without re-verification. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, leaning high.
